input.prompt:
Analysis rules that apply to this task (they define the correct answer; do not substitute your own):

R1. The corpus is the directory `corpora/repo_ledgerline/`. Every path below is relative to the
    task-set root.
R2. Consider only module-level `def` statements inside `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/`.
    Nested functions, lambdas, methods and class bodies are out of scope. There are none in
    this corpus, so this rule is a tie-breaker, not a task.
R3. Files under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/tests/` are NOT part of the analysis. Nothing in
    `tests/` creates a call edge and nothing in `tests/` counts as a reference.
R4. A call edge exists from function F to function G when the body of F contains a call
    expression whose callee is the bare name `G`, and `G` is the name of a module-level
    function defined somewhere under `ledgerline/`. Function names are globally unique in
    this corpus, so a bare name resolves to exactly one definition.
R5. Text inside a comment, a docstring or a string literal is NOT code. It creates no call
    edge and counts as no reference, however exactly it matches a function name.
R6. `ledgerline/dynamic.py` resolves handlers from strings via `getattr`. Those strings create
    no call edges.
R7. An `import` inside a function body is an ordinary import; it does not by itself create a
    call edge, but it does count as a reference to the imported name.
R8. Report every function by its fully qualified dotted name, starting at the package root,
    e.g. `ledgerline.storage.raw.execute_raw_sql`.

TASK

`ledgerline.storage.raw.execute_raw_sql` is the only function in this repository that reaches
the database directly. A reviewer wants to know which parts of the service surface can end up
executing raw SQL, however indirectly.

A function F *reaches* `execute_raw_sql` if there is a chain of one or more call edges
F -> ... -> `execute_raw_sql`. `execute_raw_sql` itself does not count.

List every function that (a) reaches `execute_raw_sql`, and (b) is defined in the packages
`ledgerline/api/`, `ledgerline/plugins/` or `ledgerline/cli/`.

Note that a similarly named function exists elsewhere in the repository. It is a different
function and paths through it do not count unless they independently reach
`execute_raw_sql`.

Output format (strict): reply with a single JSON object and nothing else - no prose before or
after it, no markdown code fence.

{
  "reaching_functions": ["<fully qualified name>", "..."],
  "count": <integer, equal to the length of reaching_functions>
}

`reaching_functions` must be sorted lexicographically ascending and must contain no duplicates.

expected_behavior: The run reads enough of the corpus to build a call graph across module boundaries, computes the reverse transitive closure from the named sink, filters that closure to the three named packages, and emits a single strict JSON object with a sorted, de-duplicated list of fully qualified names plus a count equal to the list length. A correct run distinguishes the sink from its similarly named neighbour, ignores the `getattr` dispatch table and every docstring mention of the sink, and excludes `tests/`. No file is written and no file in the corpus is modified.
quality_metric: Let K be the answer-key set and P the set in `reaching_functions`, both compared as exact case-sensitive strings. TP=|P n K|, FP=|P \ K|, FN=|K \ P|. precision=TP/(TP+FP) (defined as 0 when TP+FP=0), recall=TP/(TP+FN), quality_score = F1 = 2*precision*recall/(precision+recall), 0 when precision+recall=0, rounded to 4 decimal places. A duplicate entry is removed before scoring and is not an error. `count` disagreeing with the length of the de-duplicated list subtracts 0.05 from quality_score (floor 0). task_success = true iff quality_score >= 0.95 * (baseline C0 median quality_score for A-001) AND the run reports zero fabricated symbols.
failure_condition: Outright failure if any of: (1) Any reported symbol that is not a module-level function actually defined under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/` is a fabricated symbol. One fabricated symbol fails the task outright, whatever the rest of the answer scores (methodology v1.0.0 section 6, workload A zero-tolerance criterion). (2) the reply is not parseable as a single JSON object with the two required keys; (3) any corpus file is modified; (4) the answer is produced without reading the corpus (empty tool-call record).
notes: The answer set is large enough that the reverse closure must actually be computed; the packages in scope split close to evenly between reaching and non-reaching functions, so answering "all of them" or "none of them" scores near 0.5 F1, not near 1.0.
